newsitem.title: USA: Sonus and Abbott extend allliance.
newsitem.headline: Sonus and Abbott extend allliance.

text.p: Sonus Pharmaceuticals Inc and Abbott Laboratories Inc said they signed a second agreement under which Abbott assumes primary responsibility for all marketing, sales, and technical support of EchoGen in Europe, Latin America, Canada, Middle East, Africa, and certain Asia/Pacific Rim countries.
EchoGen is a proprietary ultrasound contrast agent developed by Sonus.
Abbott has agreed to pay Sonus $34.6 million in license and milestone payments for the international territory, a portion of which will be credited against future royalties.

In addition, Abbott has agreed to pay Sonus a royalty that ranges from 36 percent to 42 percent of EchoGen net sales based on annual sales. The agreement spans the life of the patents relating to EchoGen in the countries of the territory.
In May, Sonus and Abbott signed a strategic alliance for EchoGen in the United States. Daiichi Pharmaceutical Co Ltd has the rights to EchoGen in Japan and nine other Pacific Rim countries.

Under the agreement, Sonus has primary responsibility for clinical development and regulatory affairs for EchoGen in the European Community. Abbott has all necessary clinical development and regulatory affairs in the international territory outside the EC.

Sonus said it will use the $97.6 million in total potential license fees and milestone payments and the $15 million in related equity purchases from these agreements primarily to continue to focus on EchoGen clinical development and regulatory approval, and on new products.

Sonus said on September 5, 1996 that a New Drug Application for EchoGen had been submitted to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Sonus plans to file an application for approval of EchoGen with the European Medicines Evaluation Agency by year-end.

EchoGen is the first fluorocarbon-based ultrasound contrast agent and is being studied for use in both cardiology and radiology applications. Contrast agents are administered to patients immediately prior to imaging procedures to enhance the pictures being taken.
Sonus develops proprietary contrast agents for use in ultrasound imaging.
